subject: CareGate DPA: model-use carveouts, exportability & evidence
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Susan Park <susan.park@caregatehealth.com>, CareGate Procurement <procurement@caregatehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: CareGate DPA: model-use carveouts & exportability

Susan — great to chat this morning. Per our call, attached is a short summary of the DPA points you flagged (no-training, output entitlements, and export lane options). High level: we can commit to operational controls that prevent training on CareGate tenant data and provide an onshore export path for response bundles.

Two asks from you to make the redline executable:
- Confirm scope: is the no-train request for all CareGate production traffic or limited to PII/PHI?
- Preferred export mechanism: SFTP to your onshore partner, or API-based archive?

I looped Neha (privacy) to scope the legal language and produce an evidence pack for procurement. I expect a redline back within 48 business hours once Neha confirms the exact language.

Attachments: CareGate_Data_Questions.pdf (1 page)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if you want to run the redline together.

—Marissa

From: Susan Park <susan.park@caregatehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: CareGate Procurement <procurement@caregatehealth.com>
Date: 2025-10-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CareGate DPA: model-use carveouts & exportability

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the note. A few clarifications from procurement and security: 

1) No-training scope: CareGate requires a contractual "no-training" commitment that covers any use of customer content (including prompts and responses) for model improvement or training. We understand there may be limits (e.g., aggregated telemetry), but we need explicit language that customer content is not used to train models.

2) Output / response ownership: We need assurance that CareGate retains ownership of responses generated from our prompts for customer support transcripts and analytics. Not claiming exclusivity on model weights, but want clear output entitlements in the DPA.

3) Evidence & proof: Security will need an evidence package demonstrating how you operationalize the no-train promise (logs, KV cache purging, KV retention policy, and where logs reside). We will need this to complete our vendor risk assessment.

4) Exportability: Our legal prefers an onshore SFTP export lane for full interaction transcripts (monthly), plus an API snapshot option for ad-hoc retrieval. Also need to confirm that backups and telemetry are not replicated to training pipelines.

Please loop in privacy/legal and send a redline we can run through procurement. We are targeting an exec-signed DPA in the week of 10/20.

Best,
Susan Park
Head of Product Operations, CareGate Health

Subject: Re: CareGate DPA: model-use carveouts & exportability

Team — forwarding CareGate asks (no-train across customer content, output entitlements, evidence pack, onshore SFTP/export). Proposed approach below; please reply with any blocking concerns before I craft a DPA redline.

Proposed compromise (operational + contractual):
- Contract language: explicit "no-training" clause that prevents use of CareGate tenant data for model training or improvement. Include definition: "tenant data" = customer prompts, files, responses, and associated metadata.
- Operational proofs: quarterly evidence pack + one-time ops checklist demonstrating KV purge, prefix caching configuration, and retention windows. Evidence will include sanitized logs and an ops runbook (no raw transcripts in training pipelines).
- Export lane: monthly SFTP export (onshore) plus API snapshot for ad-hoc; retention and SLA to be defined in an annex.
- KMS: offer customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) for onshore SFTP archive if legal requires it; otherwise we can provide onshore KMS with audit logs.

Open questions:
1) Can we accept a broad "no-training" on all tenant data, or do we need carveouts for aggregated telemetry used strictly for runtime performance (not model improvement)?
2) What evidence format is acceptable to CareGate security (redacted logs vs attestation letter)?

I attached an internal checklist of evidence items to include in the pack (evidence_requirements.md – stub).

-David, Karthik — PTAL on indemnity/limitation language and whether we should insist on a scoped exception for non-personal aggregated usage.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor | Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0123

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-13T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CareGate DPA: model-use carveouts & exportability

Neha — quick notes from legal/ops review:
- We can accept a full no-train commitment for CareGate tenant data. Recommend explicit phrasing that no customer content will be used to train or improve any model weights or downstream model products.
- Carveout: allow use of aggregated non-identifiable telemetry for service quality (latency, error rates) with a clause that such telemetry will never be used to change model parameters. This balances product monitoring needs with their ask.
- Evidence: propose a three-part delivery: (1) technical runbook (how purge and prefix cache work), (2) sanitized sample logs and retention policy, (3) legal attestation letter signed by Redwood security. That should satisfy procurement/security.
- KMS/Export: OK to offer onshore SFTP export + API snapshot. If CareGate wants BYOK for archives, we need a short operational SLA for key handoff and rotation.

Karthik — confirm whether the indemnity/limitation language needs tightening if we accept full no-train. I think we can keep standard limitation language but add a narrow clause protecting us for customer-provided data quality.

I'll draft the redline and evidence pack items; Neha, happy to review before we send externally.

—David
David Kim | VP, Legal & Trust
david_kim@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: 2025-10-14T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CareGate DPA: model-use carveouts & exportability

Susan — thanks for the clear asks and the procurement checklist. Attached is a redlined DPA and a short evidence summary that maps to the items you requested. Summary of what we can commit to contractually and operationally: 

1) No-training: Redwood will not use CareGate tenant data (prompts, files, responses, or associated metadata) to train, fine-tune, or improve any models. We propose the exact clause in the redline (see Section 4.2.b).

2) Output entitlements: CareGate retains exclusive rights to outputs (responses) generated from their prompts for their internal use and downstream customer-facing products. DPA tracks language in Section 5.

3) Evidence pack: enclosed evidence_pack_summary.xlsx lists the deliverables (technical runbook, sanitized sample logs, retention policy, and a signed attestation from Redwood Security). We can produce the full pack within 5 business days of DPA signature or as an interim attestation for procurement review.

4) Export lane: we offer monthly onshore SFTP export and an API snapshot option. If CareGate requests BYOK for the export archive, we can support that under an operational SLA (annex).

Next steps: please review the redline and return any edits. I included a DocuSign link for the standard DPA if the redline is acceptable (link below). If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute handoff with Security next week to walk through the evidence pack.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign/ABCD-CARE-GATE-2025

Regards,
